title: AI Express flyer's pistol 'accidentally' goes off at Varanasi airport; 2 injured
content: Two security screeners were injured at Varanasi airport on Sunday morning. A passenger's licensed pistol accidentally discharged during a routine weapons check. The incident occurred while the passenger was preparing to board a flight to Mumbai. Both injured personnel received immediate medical treatment for their wounds. Local police are currently investigating the exact circumstances of the accidental discharge.

title: UP officers invoke Bhagat Singh, Buddha to explain duty, justice and use of force
content: During the Independence Day celebrations in Uttar Pradesh, two officers reflected on public service and the importance of accountability. One officer referenced Bhagat Singh to address the frustrations surrounding the justice system's inefficiencies. The other drew from a Gautama Buddha story to discuss the responsible use of police authority, emphasizing that with greater power comes a duty to prioritize service over personal interests and mere salary considerations.

title: US immigration authority: These forms will be rejected from September 15
content: USCIS will introduce new editions of immigration forms I-539 and I-765. These revised forms will be effective starting September 15, 2026. Applications submitted using older forms after this date will be rejected. This change aligns with a recently published immigration rule. USCIS emphasizes there will be no grace period for this form update.

title: TMC leader's suicide: CM Suvendu vows probe into possible 'threat' angle
content: Asish Banerjee Banerjee was found dead on Sunday morning at a Trinamool Congress office in Rampurhat, Birbhum district. Police said his body was found hanging and was sent for post-mortem examination. The exact circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear. A teacher by profession, Banerjee had represented the Rampurhat Assembly constituency five times. TMC legislator Kunal Ghosh called for an impartial probe.

title: PV Sindhu turns to sports science, S&C in bid for record sixth Worlds medal
content: PV Sindhu won her biggest title since 2019 at the Japan Open earlier this year. There has been a gradual improvement in results and as she goes for a record sixth BWF World Championships medal, the focus is not just on what's happening on the court. The 31-year-old has turned to sports science and a strength & conditionining team to iron out the chinks in her armour.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's donations have enabled medical debt abolition across America. Her model allows acquiring debt at low costs and then forgiving it. This approach has inspired other billionaires to contribute millions to similar causes. While philanthropic efforts are scaling, policy reforms for medical debt remain stalled. Scott's work highlights immediate relief possibilities and the need for systemic change.

title: Virginia swamp re-wetting traps 200,000 tons of carbon a year
content: North Carolina is restoring its coastal peatlands by bringing water back to areas damaged by drainage, farming and timber activities. The projects aim to reduce the risk of severe peat fires while keeping carbon stored in wet soils. At Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge, 37,000 acres have been restored, with water-control structures helping recreate natural water movement. Similar work at Angola Bay Game Land is restoring ditched peatland and wetland habitat. The efforts also support wildlife, improve resilience to flooding and sea-level rise, and involve local communities and landowners in managing water across the coastal landscape.

title: Elon Musk makes a promise to employees at townhall
content: SpaceX aims to enhance its AI model Grok by integrating insights from its workforce. Elon Musk envisions this initiative as a means to embed human values deeply into the AI's framework. Employees are not only invited to enhance the internal AI systems but are also inspired to share their expertise.

title: For 12 remote villages near China border, power is finally in sight
content: Remote villages in Uttarakhand's Johar Valley will soon receive grid electricity for the first time. This significant development will benefit approximately 180 seasonal residents and ITBP personnel stationed there. The electrification project, costing Rs 21 crore, spans sixty-one kilometers and includes twelve villages. Power lines have been laid up to Rasgadi, with Bugdiyar also slated for electrification shortly.

title: Market recap: Top 5 firms lose Rs 1 lakh cr in value; TCS, Reliance suffer biggest hit
content: Last week witnessed a downturn in Indian stock markets, with five out of the top ten firms experiencing notable decreases in market capitalization. TCS and Reliance Industries led the decline in valuations. In contrast, LIC and Bharti Airtel reported impressive gains. Despite these fluctuations, Reliance Industries held its position as the leading firm in terms of market value.

title: How members of England’s 1939 Chess Olympiad team became wartime codebreakers
content: As World War II erupted in 1939, England’s chess team withdrew from the Buenos Aires Olympiad. In Grandmaster Aarav Dengla’s fourth column for TOI, he explores how three players, Hugh Alexander, Stuart Milner-Barry, and Harry Golombek, returned home to join Bletchley Park. Harnessing chessboard skills like pattern recognition and strategic elimination, they played pivotal roles in cracking Germany’s Enigma code, helping secure Allied victory while keeping their wartime contributions secret for decades.

title: 'Awarapan 2' box office day 3: Movie set to cross Rs 70 crore on Sunday
content: The box office success of Emraan Hashmi's 'Awarapan 2' continues impressively, with the film crossing the fifty-seven crore rupees mark in India. On its third day, it grossed four point seven one crore rupees, bringing its overall net collection to over sixty crore rupees. It maintains a commanding lead against rival films in cinemas. Read on to know more in detail.

title: Cauvery water row: SC to hear Tamil Nadu plea against Karnataka on August 17
content: Tamil Nadu approached the top court on August 3, arguing that it was not receiving its allocated share of Cauvery water despite the state facing a rain-deficient year. The state government has alleged that both the quantity recommended for release by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee and the actual water supplied by Karnataka were far below its requirement.

title: ‘Very embarrassing’: Ponting tears apart Australia after Bangladesh shock
content: Bangladesh made history by defeating Pat Cummins' Australian team by nine wickets, prompting former Aussie captains Ricky Ponting and Matthew Hayden to advocate for significant team alterations. With the selectors facing mounting pressure to rejuvenate the faltering Australian side, Hayden proposed adding Sam Konstas and Matt Renshaw to strengthen the lineup. This match is notable as it marks Australia's first Test loss to Bangladesh on their own soil.

title: India cooks up LPG safety net: Govt fixes refinery-wise output targets
content: India is establishing production benchmarks for its refineries and upstream firms, aimed at fortifying the domestic LPG supply system. Reliance Industries leads with the highest targets assigned to its refinery. It is imperative that companies ensure sufficient infrastructure for LPG storage and transportation. These production benchmarks will undergo reviews and updates biannually.

title: 'Makes my blood boil': CJP seeks arrest of Bengal student's father's killers
content: The founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, Abhijeet Dipke, has expressed his support for Abdul in the wake of his father's tragic death, calling for immediate arrests. Abdul had previously highlighted the dismal state of government schools before his family suffered an assault. Dipke claims the attackers have connections to the BJP and promises continued support from CJP for justice.

title: Bizman climbs car bonnet to stop girlfriend leaving with friend, falls to death
content: A 34-year-old businessman tragically died after falling from a moving car's bonnet.  This incident occurred near AIIMS Raipur following an argument with his girlfriend.  He sustained severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the hospital.  Police are investigating the unnatural death and examining CCTV footage.  Further legal action will be taken based on collected evidence and reports.

title: 'Team didn’t have confidence in me': Jadeja’s candid revelation that left him 'disturbed'
content: Ravindra Jadeja opened up about the challenges he faced early in his career regarding his batting position. He acknowledged that batting lower in the order deeply impacted his confidence and self-belief. Jadeja noted that the team's lack of trust in his batting capabilities contributed to his struggles. His reflections came on the heels of India’s impressive Day 1, highlighted by Devdutt Padikkal achieving his first Test century against Sri Lanka.

title: Raja Sen dies at 70: Three-time National Award-winning filmmaker passes away
content: Legendary Bengali filmmaker Raja Sen departed this world on Sunday at the age of seventy. Renowned for his exceptional contributions to cinema, he was a proud recipient of three National Film Awards. Sen was receiving treatment for health issues at Kolkata's SSKM Hospital. His journey in the industry began in television before making a significant impact in feature films. He leaves behind his beloved wife and two daughters.

title: Navy sailor, wife and 2 children found dead at Mumbai home
content: A sailor and his two young children were discovered deceased at their Mumbai residence. Preliminary findings suggest the sailor died by suicide, while the children may have been poisoned. Police have initiated a thorough investigation into the tragic incident. Post-mortem and forensic reports are awaited for confirmation of causes. Investigators are gathering statements from witnesses to establish the sequence of events.

title: 'Entering politics was mistake': Mamata aide Asish Banerjee's suicide note surfaces
content: Former Trinamool Congress MLA Asish Banerjee was found dead at his party office. A suicide note was discovered, which reportedly mentioned his political journey. Banerjee had served as a five-time MLA and held ministerial portfolios. He stepped down from a party committee after losing his seat. His body was taken for a post-mortem examination.

title: 11, including 7 kids, fall ill; 3 in ICU after dead lizard found in cake near Mumbai
content: Eleven individuals suffered suspected food poisoning after consuming a birthday cake. Three children are currently in the intensive care unit receiving treatment. The children reported finding a dead lizard inside the cake they ate. Police have seized cake samples from Chamunda Cake Shop for testing. All patients are reported to be in stable condition at the hospital.

title: Holding a rally without permission? New Karnataka bill proposes jail term
content: In an effort to maintain safety during public events, Karnataka is drafting new rules that could impose fines and elevate penalties to three years in prison for unauthorized protests. The proposed legislative measures aim to bolster crowd control and reduce risks of stampedes. Notably, certain events, including weddings and funeral processes, will be exempt, emphasizing a commitment to both public order and the preservation of individual freedoms.

title: Desi CEO who sacked 900 over call gets fired himself
content: Indian-American entrepreneur Vishal Garg has been ousted as Better Home & Finance CEO.  The company cited concerns about his judgment and credibility after significant losses.  Garg's removal follows his controversial 2021 mass layoff of 900 employees.  He is now seeking to regain his position and is offering to work for one dollar annually.  Better's market value has significantly decreased since its pandemic-era peak.

title: Who is Antara Banerjee? Actress held over alleged train clash, razor attack
content: Model and actress Antara Banerjee was arrested following an alleged train confrontation.  She was traveling towards Surat for a shoot with a sleeper-class ticket.  Railway personnel intervened after a dispute arose over her seating in an AC coach.  Allegations include assaulting public servants and causing harm during the incident.  Banerjee was later released on bail after being deboarded.

title: How Bangladesh followed Virat Kohli's template to humble Australia in Darwin
content: What began with Virat Kohli's call for greater investment in Test cricket and India's formidable pace attack became a blueprint for Bangladesh. Mominul Haque transformed the domestic system, backed fast bowlers and changed the country's Test cricket culture. Hasan Mahmud's six-wicket haul against Australia is now proof that the gamble is paying off.

title: 'She fell from roof': BSF jawan told family after wife's murder; arrested
content: A Border Security Force jawan was arrested for allegedly murdering his wife in Punjab.  The victim's father filed a complaint after his daughter was found dead with injuries.  He stated his daughter faced harassment and physical assault from her husband after marriage.  The jawan claimed his wife fell from the roof, but the FIR alleges she was beaten.  Police have arrested the accused jawan and are continuing their investigation.

title: From GST reform to GCCs: How India can become a $20 trillion economy by 2036
content: India could reach a $20 trillion economy by 2036 with reforms. Services will drive this expansion, contributing over 65% of the GDP. A 20-step reform agenda targets taxes and capital markets for efficiency. Global capability centers and tourism offer significant growth opportunities. Successful execution of these measures is crucial for achieving the target.

title: PMAY-U 2.0: Kerala's 30,000 beneficiaries may get Rs 4 lakh housing assistance
content: Kerala's Cabinet has officially greenlit the second phase of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban 2.0, paving the way for around 30,000 eligible beneficiaries to gain significant housing aid. The state plans to ink a Memorandum of Understanding with the Central government, which will unlock Rs 450 crore in financial support for this housing initiative. The completion of phase one is projected for September 2026.

title: The trouble with getting used to miracles
content: Modern technology works so well it becomes invisible to users.  This invisibility makes critical thinking about scientific claims essential today.  We must ask how we know things and what evidence supports them.  Developing disciplined curiosity is a necessary defense against misinformation.  Looking at familiar things from new angles offers valuable perspective.

title: Hungary bus crash: 12 killed, 10 injured after Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway

Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced the tragic casualties on Facebook. He also expressed his sincere condolences to the families of the victims. The exact cause of the accident remains unknown at this time.

title: 'Who is he saluting?' RJD mocks Nishant Kumar over flag-hoisting gesture - video
content:
RJD targets Nishant Kumar over flag-hoisting video, asks ‘who is he saluting?’

The Rashtriya Janata Dal on Sunday targeted Bihar health minister Nishant Kumar by sharing a video of him hoisting the Tricolour on Independence Day. The Lalu Yadav-led party mocked former chief minister Nitish Kumar’s son over his gesture shortly after the flag-hoisting. Posting the video on its official account, the RJD asked, “Who is the health minister saluting?” Taking its attack further, the main opposition party in Bihar said, “And to whom is he turning his back?” JD(U) leader Nishant Kumar, the son of Bihar’s longest-serving chief minister, has repeatedly come under the opposition’s scrutiny over his gestures on several occasions. Nishant Kumar was inducted into the state Cabinet soon after Samrat Choudhary became chief minister, replacing Nitish Kumar. Nitish subsequently became a Rajya Sabha member, marking the end of the Lalu-Nitish era in Bihar.

End of Article

content: The bus ran into a ditch and tipped over early on Sunday near the town of Mezokeresztes in eastern Hungary, police said, adding that the bus was heading towards the city of Nyiregyhaza on the motorway when the accident happened.

title: 'She Fell From Roof': Border Force Jawan Tells Family After Killing Wife In Punjab

content: Ukraine has been carrying out strikes deep inside Russia in recent weeks, with drone barrages targeting military, industrial and more recently e-commerce warehouses far from the front line in the war that is in its fifth year.

title: Asish Banerjee, Mamata Banerjee's Close Aide, Found Dead At Trinamool Office

title: ‘Entire Bengal fuming’: Suvendu Adhikari slams Sonia Gandhi over I-Day Vande Mataram row
content: chief minister suvendu Adhikari slams parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi . he also accuses the Congress of indulging in "appeasement politics" the row erupted after visuals showed senior Congress leaders speaking among themselves while Vande Mataram was being recited .

title: Over 100 arrested in Morocco over fresh Ceuta migrant crossing attempt
content: around 111 people arrested in ceuta for attempting another border crossing . the arrests came about two weeks after a large influx of migrants reached Ceutan . 109 of those arrested were from sub-Saharan Africa and two were Moroccan nationals .

title: ‘Feeding my friends’: PM Modi’s quiet Independence Day morning with cows, peacocks
content: the pm shared a glimpse of his morning routine on twitter . he said feeding the animals was part of his daily routine . the video showed him spending time with the animals at his 7, Lok Kalyan Marg residence before departing for the historic monument .

title: Can reputation of a celebrity be inherited, asks HC
content: the HC questioned whether a family's reputation flows down generations, how far personality rights extend and whether even "egregiously despicable" fake news can violate intellectual property rights . in 2023, a single-judge bench had restrained several YouTube channels from publishing misleading content on Aaradhya's health .

title: 'Didn't call opposition leaders dimagi naxals': Rijiju on PM Modi's I-Day remarks
content: "dimagi naxals" referred only to those who supported Maoists and rejected Indian Constitution . "who want to cut chicken neck to separate North-East from India," he said . parliamentary affairs minister says the remarks are not meant for opposition leaders .

title: Bangladesh PM's proposed India visit conditional on Hasina extradition, officials say
content: the comments came as speculation grew over whether Rahman would travel to India later this month for his first official visit since becoming prime minister . he said that the necessary conditions for such a visit had yet to be established . title: At BCI helm for 14 years, Manan Kumar Mishra faces heat over professional conduct
content: a statutory body established under Advocates Act, 1961, is mandated to regulate legal profession and legal education . it lays down standards of professional conduct for advocates, exercises disciplinary jurisdiction, and recognises universities whose law degrees qualify a person for enrolment . but no provision of the Act gives it the power to admit persons as advocates on its roll .

title: Maggie Walz came to Michigan with $7, later founded a 1,000-person colony
